subject: Fire Station Maintenance and Firefighter Cancer Prevention
overview: The Council addressed hazardous structural conditions at local fire stations and mandated the immediate purchase of gear-washing extractors to reduce cancer risks for firefighters. Members also initiated the development of a new exterior lighting ordinance and demanded accountability for substandard road restoration by public utilities.

items.title: Fire Station Maintenance and Specialized Equipment
items.summary: Approved a multi-part resolution calling for repairs to the deteriorating floor at Engine 3, the immediate purchase of two turnout gear extractors to mitigate cancer risks, and a city-wide inspection of fire station safety systems. The Council also scheduled a Committee of the Whole tour of all fire facilities to prioritize maintenance needs in the upcoming budget.

items.title: Exterior Lighting Ordinance Referral
items.summary: Referred a request to the Subcommittee on Zoning and Ordinances to develop regulations for outdoor light wattage and luminance to protect neighborhoods from the glare of new developments.

items.title: Street Resurfacing and Utility Accountability
items.summary: Approved requests for construction schedules for Evans and Paris Streets and a detailed report identifying where public utilities have failed to restore roadways to city standards after excavation.

items.title: Ceremonial Resolutions and Condolences
items.summary: Adopted a congratulatory resolution for Phyllis Patton’s 80th birthday and held a moment of silence for former teacher and coach Jim Coughlin.

items.title: Veterans Memorial Park Plaque Update
items.summary: Placed on file the eligibility requirements for adding names to the Winthrop Street Veterans Memorial and requested a reverse 911 call to notify the public of the March 15 application deadline.

items.title: Routine Announcements
items.summary: Heard announcements regarding an upcoming community police meeting, a Board of Appeals meeting for the Salem and Canal Street project, and a charity road race.

items.title: Police Station Bond Committee Report
items.summary: Accepted a report from the Committee of the Whole regarding the police station bond order and prior questions.

items.title: Petition for Revised Proclamation
items.summary: Placed on file a resident’s proposed alternative proclamation addressing Medford's history with colonialism and abolitionism.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the meeting records for February 14 and February 28, 2017, with clerical corrections.

items.title: Public Comment on Police Station Costs
items.summary: A resident questioned the $1.7 million architect fees for the proposed police station, prompting the Council to clarify that a third reading on the matter is scheduled for March 21.
